description: Whenever the Attorney General has reasonable cause to believe that any person has engaged in, is engaging in, or is about to engage in any violation of this chapter, the Attorney General is empowered to issue a civil investigative demand; § 59.1-9.10 applies mutatis mutandis.

Prior to initiating any action, the Attorney General shall provide a controller or processor 30 days' written notice identifying the specific provisions of this chapter alleged to have been or being violated.

If within the 30-day period the controller or processor cures the noticed violation and provides the Attorney General an express written statement that the alleged violations have been cured and that no further violations shall occur, no action shall be initiated.
The Attorney General may initiate an action in the name of the Commonwealth and may seek an injunction to restrain any violations of this chapter.

Civil penalties of up to $7,500 for each violation under this chapter, payable into the state treasury and credited to the Regulatory, Consumer Advocacy, Litigation, and Enforcement Revolving Trust Fund.

type: Recovery of Expenses and Attorney Fees
description: The Attorney General may recover reasonable expenses incurred in investigating and preparing the case, including attorney fees, in any action initiated under this chapter.

Where a controller denies a consumer's appeal, the controller shall provide the consumer with an online mechanism, if available, or other method through which the consumer may contact the Attorney General to submit a complaint.
